clue.text: Smell like items of underwear

parts.note: a tang is a sharp smell or taste
as means like, in the same way

explanation.surface: Someone observes that some underwear smells.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangas are skimpy briefs, a kind of knickers.

clue.text: Gangster and US president sharing the same characteristics

parts.note: Al Capone is the archetypal gangster
Ike was the nickname of President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A mobster and a president turn out to be peas in a pod.
explanation.definitionFit: Similar things have features in common.

clue.text: Hear Margaret is a welcoming type

indicators.note: hear tells us the answer sounds like the name rather than being spelt the same

parts.note: Greta is a short form of Margaret

explanation.surface: Listen: Margaret is a friendly sort.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic (British) accent the name GRETA sounds just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who welcomes visitors at a door is a host who says hello.

clue.text: Sister can keep order, it's plain

indicators.note: keep means hold within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: A nun can maintain discipline, it's obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour, an 'order' to crossword setters; 'can' and 'it's' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Sober colours are plain and unshowy.

clue.text: New clothes for cash

definitions.meaning: a fresh set of garments to put on, as in a spare outfit
loose coins, money handed back after a purchase

explanation.definitionFit: A change of clothes is a fresh outfit, and coins are small money.

clue.text: Cycle with Welshman on northbound road in Scotland

parts.note: c is the abbreviation for cycle, as in cycles per second
Aled is a Welsh man's name, as in the singer Aled Jones

indicators.note: northbound in a down clue means read upwards, so the road is reversed

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's Great North Road, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A cyclist rides north with a Welsh companion on the road into Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 runs from London to Edinburgh; 'northbound' reverses AI to IA in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia is the old Latin name for the northern part of Britain.

clue.text: Tree: a Roman statesman's right at the top

indicators.note: at the top says the letter is shifted to the head of the word

parts.note: Brutus was the Roman statesman who helped assassinate Caesar

explanation.surface: A tree: a Roman statesman has his rightful place at the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the top' moves the R of BRUTUS to the front, giving RBUTUS after A.
explanation.definitionFit: The arbutus is the strawberry tree, an evergreen shrub.

clue.text: Ghost with arms a flutter at night

definitions.text: Ghost with arms a flutter at night

indicators.note: a flutter suggests letters agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A phantom flaps its arms in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a flutter' rearranges GHOST plus ARMS; the whole clue also describes a pale insect fluttering at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass moths are pale night-flying insects that flutter up from lawns.

clue.text: Alternative course of action, a bit of a fiddle

definitions.meaning: a backup plan or substitute option
a part of a violin, one of its four strings

explanation.definitionFit: A fallback option is a reserve plan, and a violin has a string next to the top one.

clue.text: Former priest turned on victim of ban

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife

indicators.note: turned tells us to read the priest's name backwards

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: An ex-priest has turned against the person who was banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses ELI to ILE; 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone banished from their country is the casualty of a banning order.

clue.text: Charge committee for advertising space

parts.note: a bill is a charge for goods or services
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A committee is billed for the hoarding it put up.
explanation.definitionFit: A large outdoor hoarding where posters are pasted is advertising space.

clue.text: Play that ran in the West End for such a long time?

definitions.text: Play that ran in the West End
definitions.meaning: a Michael Frayn comedy staged in London's theatre district
an idiom for ages, an extremely long period

explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre district; Michael Frayn's comedy was staged there in 1976.
explanation.definitionFit: Frayn's comedy title is also a British idiom meaning ages.

clue.text: It's clear one will get ruddy exhausted

parts.note: overt means plain to see, clear
I is the Roman numeral for one
ruddy means red in colour

explanation.surface: Someone observes that a person will obviously end up bloody worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruddy' reads as the British mild swear word, but here it simply means red.
explanation.definitionFit: Being past the point of tiredness is to be utterly drained.

clue.text: Boxer having match, say, with lad

indicators.note: say tells us to take the word as it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a tie is a match between teams, as in a cup tie
a son is a lad, a male child

explanation.surface: A boxer has a fight with a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns TIE into its sound TY; in Britain a 'cup tie' is a knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Tyson was a world heavyweight champion fighter.

clue.text: Remonstrated with pet, running wild in shop

indicators.note: running wild says the letters charge about out of order

explanation.surface: Someone argued with their pet as it ran amok in a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running wild' shuffles REMONSTRATED plus PET; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A large retail store selling many kinds of goods in separate sections is a type of shop.

clue.text: Payment for work that's needed in carpet weaving, note

indicators.note: needed in says these letters must go into the other piece
weaving says the letters are interlaced into a new pattern

parts.note: i.e. is short for id est, that is
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Payment for labour required when weaving a carpet, take note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weaving' rearranges CARPET to PCERAT; 'needed in' puts IE inside it after the P, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Being paid per item produced is a pay system based on output.

clue.text: German composer and Mister Porter possibly entertaining a viewer

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: an eye is something that views
porter is a dark beer, so beer is the wider category

explanation.surface: A German composer and a Mr Porter are hosting a spectator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter possibly' looks like a surname; porter is a type of beer, the 'possibly' marking an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Meyerbeer was a German-born opera composer.

clue.text: One-time headline about Agatha Christie thriller?

definitions.text: One-time headline about Agatha Christie thriller?

parts.words: One-time headline about Agatha Christie thriller
parts.note: in 1926 the crime writer disappeared for eleven days, and a newspaper might have announced her disappearance in the words of a famous Hitchcock film title

explanation.surface: A newspaper banner from the past about a Christie whodunnit.
explanation.walkthrough: Christie's real disappearance in 1926 made front pages; the answer is the title of a 1938 Hitchcock thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a 1938 Hitchcock thriller would suit a report of the author's disappearance.

clue.text: See me break into an old car in tree-lined avenue

parts.note: a is the same as an

indicators.note: break into says the word forces its way inside the other piece

parts.note: the Lada is a Soviet-era car marque

explanation.surface: Watch me burgle an old banger parked on a leafy boulevard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lada was a cheap Russian car often mocked in Britain; 'See' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An alameda is a public walk shaded by trees, a Spanish-style promenade.

clue.text: Group of swimmers enjoyed plunge

indicators.note: Group of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A swimming club had a good time taking a dip.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge something into liquid is to submerge it.

clue.text: Polish girl's anger towards North America

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: A Polish girl's fury is aimed at America.
explanation.definitionFit: Irena is a common female name in Poland.

clue.text: Possibly more scope to reform?

indicators.note: possibly suggests these letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A question whether more room for manoeuvre would help a reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges MORE SCOPE; the answer itself means to compose again, matching the anagram idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose again is to put together afresh, to form anew.

clue.text: Worry as daughter joins in group of activists

indicators.note: joins in says one piece enters another

parts.note: care means worry, anxiety

explanation.surface: A girl is anxious as she joins a protest group.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a core group trained to lead a political movement.

definitions.meaning: a 1957 rock and roll song by Buddy Holly and the Crickets
a call addressed to a lad

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
an air is a distinctive manner or look, as in an air of mystery

explanation.surface: Bringing a playhouse's characteristic look back to life.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend something is to bring it back to working order.

clue.text: Man or woman, extremely lonely stuck in flat

indicators.note: stuck in says one piece is lodged inside another

parts.note: even means flat, level

indicators.note: extremely means take the extremes, the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone, very lonely, is trapped in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters LY of 'lonely', which go inside EVEN. 'flat' is not an apartment but means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn is a name given to both sexes, like the novelist Evelyn Waugh.
